Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145701
Court No. - 72
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 8141 of 2023
Applicant :- Rajeev Kumar Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vandana Mishra,Anjul Dwivedi,Sai Girdhar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Sai Girdhar, learned counsel for the applicant and Ms. Ifrah Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.35 of 2022, registered under Sections 409, 419 and 420 IPC at Police Station- Chetganj, District Varanasi with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant, who happens to be the Sales Manager of the company Nilgiri Infracity Private Ltd., is stated to have usurped an amount of Rs.4.5 lakhs of the informant Rajeev Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139292301/
1 and neither provided a plot nor returned the said money.

entities.text: Rajeev Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is simply an employee in the company and has nothing to do with the said offence.
He has acted at the behest of the superior authorities.
The applicant is not on the board of the directors of the company.
The person on the board of directors are Vikash Singh, Ritu Singh and Sanjay Prajapati.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no previous criminal antecedents of the applicant except the ten cases instituted regarding the same company and similar type of transactions.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
6.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

7. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.text: Rajeev Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
[Krishan Pahal, J.] Order Date :- 21.7.2023 Vikas  Rajeev Kumar Singh vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139292301/
